chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man gives charity to his children while they are young. Is it for him to retract from it? He (peace be upon him) said: No, the charity is for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
ai.seo_question: Can a father take back charity he gave to his young children?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that when a father gives *sadaqah* (voluntary charity) to his young children, it is treated as a distinct gift that becomes their exclusive property, thereby prohibiting him from revoking it. This ruling distinguishes *sadaqah* from *hibah* (gift), emphasizing that the act is for the sake of Allah and thus carries the permanence of a completed transfer of ownership, a principle widely cited in Shia jurisprudence regarding family wealth distribution.
